source: MAFF — សារៈប្រយោជន៍នៃដំណាំស្រូវ (Value of the Rice Crop) slide deck, presenter contact temseng@yahoo.com, p.9
text: Rice-derived compounds can be marketed as 'functional food' — a food product formulated and marketed for a specific health benefit beyond basic nutrition, representing a much higher value-added category than raw grain or simple snacks. The slide cites a real commercial example, a Thai product called 'NEUROFOOD' (branded 'Food for Thought'), containing 'polysaccharide-peptides' associated with rice starch (illustrated with a scanning-electron-microscope image of a starch-like particle) and marketed as supporting brain and memory function, sold in a 165 g jar. The slide also includes a clipping from the Thai newspaper The Sunday Nation profiling the product's inventor under the headline 'Innovative whiz-kid,' presented as a real-world success story of turning agricultural science into a branded health product. Note: this is a foreign (Thai) commercial example used for illustration/inspiration, not a Cambodian product — it should not be assumed to be available or replicable in Cambodia without its own R&D, regulatory approval, and investment.
